front: What is Docker Runtime Security in one sentence?
back: Shrink the container attack surface: non-root, dropped caps, seccomp, read-only rootfs — Docker Deep Dive (Poulton) + Container Security (Liz Rice).

front: Explain the mental model of Docker Runtime Security (how the system thinks).
back: A container is namespaced processes on shared kernel — not a VM. Security = defense in depth:

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Docker Runtime Security?
back: Host kernel → Default retained caps include CHOWN, NET_RAW, etc. — drop ALL, add back minimally. → Docker default seccomp profile blocks ~40 dangerous syscalls (reboot, mount, …). → Writable rootfs = attacker can drop binaries, modify /etc, install persistence. → Prevents setuid binaries from gaining privs (e.g. exploited ping setuid).

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Docker Runtime Security?
back: Default retained caps include CHOWN, NET_RAW, etc. — drop ALL, add back minimally.

front: Symptom: Permission denied writing file — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: read-only rootfs · Fix: Mount volume/tmpfs for that path

front: Symptom: Operation not permitted — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: seccomp or cap drop · Fix: Add specific cap or syscall to profile

front: Symptom: Can't bind port 80 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: non-root · Fix: Listen 8080 + reverse proxy; or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE

front: Symptom: App exits as root — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing USER · Fix: Fix Dockerfile; verify docker inspect User

front: Symptom: DNS works in dev, fails hardened — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NET_RAW dropped · Fix: Usually not needed; check outbound firewall

front: Symptom: JVM/Node crash on seccomp — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: blocked syscall in logs · Fix: Custom seccomp allowlist for runtime

front: Gotcha with Docker Runtime Security: what silently fails?
back: Mounting /var/run/docker.sock — container owns the host. CI pattern only with isolated runners.

front: When should you NOT use Docker Runtime Security?
back: Hardware/device containers (GPU, BPF loaders) — may legitimately need extra caps; document exception. seccomp-unconfined as default — only narrow debug window. Security theater — read-only rootfs while running root with --privileged undoes everything.

front: What is Docker compose in one sentence?
back: Multi-container apps as declarative YAML — docker compose v2 is a Docker CLI plugin, not a separate Python binary — Compose spec + Docker Deep Dive (Poulton).

front: Explain the mental model of Docker compose (how the system thinks).
back: Compose orchestrates one host / one stack (dev, CI, small prod). Not a cluster scheduler — that's Kubernetes.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Docker compose?
back: docker compose up → Project name = directory name (or -p) → Service name = DNS name on default network → http://api:8080 from sibling container

front: Given a broken Docker compose setup, what is your first validation command?
back: docker compose up

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Docker compose?
back: Without condition: service_healthy, depends_on only waits for container *start*, not app ready — race on first request.

front: Symptom: connection refused between services — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: docker compose ps; wrong service name · Fix: Use service name not localhost cross-container

front: Symptom: Works once, fails on restart — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: No healthcheck; app starts before DB · Fix: condition: service_healthy

front: Symptom: Config change ignored — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Old container running · Fix: docker compose up -d --force-recreate

front: Symptom: Permission denied on bind mount — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: UID mismatch (root in container) · Fix: Named volume; or user: in compose

front: Symptom: Secrets in docker inspect — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Plain environment: · Fix: Move to secrets / external secret manager

front: Symptom: Disk fills — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Bind mount logs on host · Fix: Log driver limits; named volumes; rotation

front: Symptom: port is already allocated — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Host port clash · Fix: Change ports: or stop conflicting service

front: Symptom: Prod outage after down -v — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Operator ran destructive down · Fix: Backups; document runbooks; avoid -v in prod

front: Gotcha with Docker compose: what silently fails?
back: Bind mount database data dir — SELinux (:Z), path drift, backup/restore pain, corrupt on laptop sleep. Use named volumes for state.

front: When should you NOT use Docker compose?
back: Multi-node HA, PDB, autoscaling — kubectl / Kubernetes. Secret rotation at scale — Vault, cloud SM, not flat files on disk. Compose in prod at large scale — OK for single-node edge/small SaaS; plan migration path early.

front: What is docker cli in one sentence?
back: Day-one Docker CLI for build, run, debug, and cleanup — Docker docs + on-call triage when containers misbehave.

front: Explain the mental model of docker cli (how the system thinks).
back: Image = template; container = running (or stopped) instance. Build context = everything sent to daemon during docker build (.dockerignore matters).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for docker cli?
back: Common lint failures: missing .dockerignore, latest tag in prod, root user, unpinned base image.

front: Given a broken docker cli setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Common lint failures: missing .dockerignore, latest tag in prod, root user, unpinned base image.

front: What are the production-safe defaults for docker cli?
back: Common lint failures: missing .dockerignore, latest tag in prod, root user, unpinned base image.

front: Symptom: Cannot connect to Docker daemon — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: systemctl status docker · Fix: Start daemon; user in docker group; DOCKER_HOST

front: Symptom: Build fails COPY missing file — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Context vs .dockerignore · Fix: Fix path; adjust ignore; docker build --progress=plain

front: Symptom: Container exits immediately — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: docker logs; exit code · Fix: Fix CMD; run interactively; check arch mismatch

front: Symptom: Port already allocated — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: ss -tlnp \ · Fix: grep :3000

front: Symptom: Out of disk — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: docker system df · Fix: Prune; expand volume; logs rotation

front: Symptom: Works locally, fails CI — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Platform (linux/amd64) · Fix: docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64

front: Symptom: DNS inside container broken — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: docker exec cat /etc/resolv.conf · Fix: Custom network; corporate proxy

front: Symptom: no space left on device during build — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Layer cache · Fix: Prune; multi-stage build; smaller base

front: Symptom: Network alias not resolving — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Same user-defined network? · Fix: docker network connect; use service name in compose

front: Gotcha with docker cli: what silently fails?
back: docker system prune -a --volumes in prod — deletes unused volumes including orphaned DB data.

front: When should you NOT use docker cli?
back: Production orchestration at scale — Docker compose for dev; Kubernetes/systemd for prod HA. Rootful Docker for untrusted code — use rootless mode or sandbox (Docker Runtime Security). Long-term log storage — ship to journal/Loki; docker logs rotates with container.
